questions.text: From a rectangular sheet of tin (length 6 meter, breadth 4 meter), a square of side 1.5 meter is cut from all the corners of the sheet. The remaining portion of the sheet is folded into the shape of an open box. The volume of the box in cubic meters is
questions.explanation:
Given: 

From a rectangular sheet of tin (length 6 meter, breadth 4 meter), a square of side 1.5 meter is cut from all the corners of the sheet. 

Concept Used: 

Volume of open box = l x b x h

Calculation:

⇒ The length and breadth is reduced by = 2 x 1.5 = 3 m

New length, l = 6 - 3 = 3 m

New breadth, b = 4 - 3 = 1 m

Height of open box, h = 1.5 m 

Volume of the box = l x b x h

Volume of the box = 3 x 1 x 1.5  = 4.5 m2 = 4\(\frac{1}{2}\) m3

So, the volume of the open box is  4\(\frac{1}{2}\) m3.

questions.text: The ratio of the perimeter of a rectangle and the perimeter of a square is 4 : 5, and the breadth of the rectangle is equal to the side of the square. If the length of the rectangle is 12 cm, then what is the ratio of the area of the square to the area of the rectangle ?
questions.explanation:
Length of the rectangle is 12 cm 

Breadth of the rectangle is equal to side of the square ( a = b )

Ratio of perimeter of rectangle and perimeter of square is 4 : 5

⇒2 ( L + B ) / 4A  = 4 / 5

⇒2( 12 + B ) / 4B = 4 / 5

⇒60 + 5B = 8B

⇒60 = 8B - 5B 

⇒3B = 60 

⇒B = 20cm 

Then side of the square and breadth of the rectangle is 20cm

Area of the square is 20 × 20 = 400 sq cm

Area of the rectangle is 20 × 12 = 240 sq cm

Ratio of these areas = 400 : 240 

⇒5 : 3

Hence 5 : 3 is the correct answer.

questions.text: The difference between the total surface area and lateral surface area of a cube is 288 sq cm, the length of rectangle is 41( 2/3)% more than edge of this cube. The ratio of length to breadth is 34 : 33, respectively. Then find the area of the rectangle ?
questions.explanation:
According to question,

6 × a × a - 4 × a × a = 288 sq cm

⇒2 a2 = 288

⇒a2​  = 144

⇒a = 12 cm

Length of rectangle = 12 × 17/12 [41( 2/3)% = 5/12]

Ratio of length and breadth is 34 : 33

⇒34 unit is equal to 17 cm 

Then breadth of the rectangle is 33/2 cm

Area of the rectangle is 17 cm × 33/2 cm 

⇒280.5 sq cm 

Hence 280.5 sq cm is the correct answer.

questions.text: The radius of a circle is equal to 7/8th of the side of a square. The ratio of the area of a circle and area of the rectangle is 11: 6. If the sum of the length and breadth of rectangle is 100 cm and the difference between the length and breadth of the rectangle is 40 cm, find the square's perimeter.
questions.explanation:
Given:

Radius of circle = (7/8) × Side of square

Ratio of area of circle and area of  rectangle = 11 : 6

Length of rectangle + Breadth of rectangle = 100 cm

Length of rectangle – Breadth of rectangle = 40 cm

Formula Used:

Area of circle = πr2

Area of square = side × side

Perimeter of square = 4 × side

Perimeter of circle = 2πr

Area of rectangle = length × breadth

Calculation:

Suppose the length and breadth of the rectangle is x and y, respectively.

x + y = 100

x – y = 40

So, y = (100 – 40)/2 = 30 cm

And, x = 140/2 = 70 cm

Area of rectangle = x × y

⇒ 70 × 30

⇒ 2100 sq. cm

Ratio of area of circle and area of the rectangle = 11 : 6

⇒ 6 units = 2100

⇒ 1 unit = 350

⇒ 11 units = 3850

So, the area of the circle = πr2

⇒ 22/7 × r2 = 3850

⇒ r2 = (3850 × 7/22)

⇒ r2 = 1225

⇒ r = √1225

⇒ r = 35 cm

Radius of circle = (7/8) × Side of square

⇒ 35 = (7/8) × Side of square

⇒ Side of square = 40 cm

Perimeter of the square = 4 × 40 = 160

∴ The perimeter of the square is 160 cm.

questions.text: The radius of a sphere is equal to the radius of a cone and the volume of the sphere is equal to the volume of the cone. Find the curved surface area of the sphere when the height of the cone is 28 m. (Take π = 22/7)
questions.explanation:
Given:

Radius of a sphere =  Radius of a cone

Volume of the sphere = Volume of the cone

Height of cone = 28 m

Formula used:

(1) Volume of a sphere = (4/3)πr3

(2) Volume of a cone = (1/3)πr2h

(3) Curved surface area of a sphere = 4πr2

where, r = radius and h = height

Calculation:

Let the radius of the sphere be x cm.

Then, Volume of sphere = Volume of cone

⇒ (4/3)π(x)3 = (1/3)π(x)2 × 28 cm

⇒ x = 28/4

⇒ x = 7 m

Now, Curved surface area of the sphere = 4πr2

⇒ 4 × (22/7) × 72 

⇒ 616 m2

∴ The curved surface area of the sphere is 616 m2.

questions.text: The sum of the area of two rectangles is 384 cm<sup>2 </sup>and the breadth of both rectangles is equal to the diameter of the circle whose area is 16π cm<sup>2</sup>. If the difference between the lengths of both rectangles is 24 cm, then, find the sum of the perimeter of both rectangles (in cm)?
questions.explanation:
Given:

Sum of area of both rectangle = 384 cm2

Breadth of both rectangle = Diameter of the circle

Sum of length of both rectangle = 48 cm

Formula Used:

Area of rectangle = length × breadth

Perimeter of Rectangle = 2(length + breadth)

Area of circle = πr2

Perimeter of circle = 2πr

Calculation:

Suppose the length of both rectangle is x and y, respectively.

The area of the circle = πr2 = 16π

⇒ r2 = 16

⇒ r = 4 cm

The diameter of circle = 8 cm which is equal to breadth of the rectangle.

Sum of the area of both rectangle = 384 cm2

⇒ 8x + 8y = 384

⇒ x + y = 48 cm      ---(i)

Now, the difference between the lengths of the both rectangles = 24 cm

⇒ x – y = 24 cm      ---(ii)

Add both equation (i) and (ii), we have –

⇒ 2x = 72

⇒ x = 72/2

⇒ x = 36 cm

Put this value in the equation (i), we have –

⇒ 36 + y = 48

⇒ y = 12 cm

Therefore, perimeter of the first rectangle = 2(x + 8) = 2(36 + 8)

⇒ 2(44)

⇒ 88 cm

Perimeter of the second rectangle = 2(y +8)

⇒ 2(12 + 8)

⇒ 2(20)

⇒ 40 cm

The sum of the perimeter of both rectangle = (88 + 40) cm

⇒ 128 cm

questions.text: If the volume of two cylinders is in the ratio of 1 : 3 and the radius being of 5 cm and 6 cm respectively and the difference of their height is 13 cm then find the volume of the small radius cylinder?
questions.explanation:
GIVEN:

⇒ The volume of two cylinder = 1 : 3      ----(1)

⇒ The radius of two cylinder = 5 cm and 6 cm respectively.     ----(2)

⇒ Difference of their heights = 13 cm

FORMULA USED:

⇒ Volume of cylinder = πr2h cu.cm

CALCULATION:

For cylinder 1:

⇒ 1 = π × 5 × 5 × h1      ----(1)

For cylinder 2:

⇒ 3 = π × 6 × 6 × h2      ----(2)

Dividing eq(1) by eq(2)

⇒ 1/3 = 25h1/36h2

⇒ h1/h2 = 12/25

⇒ Difference = 13x

⇒ 1x = 1 cm

⇒ Volume of small cylinder = π × 5 × 5 × 12

⇒ Volume = 300π cu.cm

questions.text: If 280 ml of water can be filled in cylindrical or conical flasks to its brim. Find the ratio of the circumference of a cylindrical to that of a conical flask, given that their height is the same.
questions.explanation:
Given

The volume of cylindrical flask = volume of the conical flask

Height of cylindrical flask = height of conical flask

Concept

The volume of cylindrical flask = πR2H, where R and H are the radius and height of the cylindrical flask

Volume of conical flask = (1/3)πr2h, where r and h are the radius and height of conical flask

Calculation

∵ The height of both flasks are the same, let the height be H

The volume of cylindrical flask/volume of conical flask = 280/280

⇒ Volume of cylindrical flask/ Volume of conical flask = π R2H/[(1/3)πr2H]

⇒ R2/[(1/3)r2] = 1

⇒ R2/r2 = 1/3

⇒ R/r = 1/√3

Circumference of cylindrical flask = 2πR

Circumference of conical flask = 2πr

The ratio of the circumference of the cylindrical flask to conical flask = 2πR/2πr

⇒ 2πR/2πr = R/r

⇒ R/r = 1/√3

⇒ The ratio of the circumference of conical to cylindrical flask = 1 ∶ √3

∴ The ratio of the circumference of a cylindrical to that of a conical flask is 1 ∶ √3
